terms.definition: A flexible EC2 pricing model where you commit to a specific dollar-per-hour spend for 1 or 3 years in exchange for up to 72% discount. Unlike Reserved Instances, it's not tied to a specific instance type.
terms.example: Committing to spend $0.041/hour on EC2 regardless of which instance type you use

terms.definition: The most flexible Savings Plan type — applies discounts across EC2 (any family, region, size, OS), AWS Fargate, and AWS Lambda. Offers up to 66% discount.
terms.example: A single plan covering both your EC2 web servers and Lambda functions

terms.definition: A Savings Plan locked to a specific instance family and region (e.g., t3 in us-east-1). Offers the deepest discount at up to 72% within that family.
terms.example: Committing to t3 instances in us-east-1 for one year

terms.definition: An EC2 instance that uses AWS spare capacity at up to 90% discount compared to On-Demand. AWS can reclaim the instance at any time with a 2-minute warning.
terms.example: Running nightly data processing jobs on Spot Instances to save costs

terms.definition: The event where AWS reclaims a Spot Instance because the capacity is needed elsewhere or the Spot price exceeds your maximum. Preceded by a 2-minute notification.
terms.example: Your Spot Instance receives an interruption notice at 2:00 PM and terminates at 2:02 PM

terms.definition: A collection of Spot Instances (and optionally On-Demand Instances) managed together across multiple instance types and AZs to meet a target capacity at minimum cost.
terms.example: A Spot Fleet using t3.large, t3.xlarge, and m5.large across three AZs for an ML training cluster

terms.definition: A console feature in EC2 that shows the historical price fluctuation of Spot Instances for a given instance type and AZ over the past 90 days.
terms.example: Checking that t3.micro prices in us-east-1a have been stable and low before committing to that pool

terms.definition: A Spot interruption behavior that saves the instance RAM contents to the encrypted EBS root volume before stopping. On restart, RAM is restored so applications resume exactly where they stopped.
terms.example: An in-memory database job resumes from exactly the same point after a Spot interruption

terms.definition: A physical EC2 server fully dedicated to your use — no other AWS customer shares the hardware. Gives visibility into physical core and socket topology for BYOL licensing.
terms.example: Running Oracle Database with per-core licensing on a Dedicated Host

terms.definition: An EC2 instance that runs on hardware dedicated to your AWS account, but without full physical server visibility or BYOL support. Provides basic physical isolation.
terms.example: A compliance-sensitive app running on hardware not shared with other companies

terms.definition: Using software licenses you already own (like Oracle, Windows Server, or SQL Server) on AWS infrastructure instead of paying AWS for new licenses.
terms.example: Moving an Oracle Database with existing per-core licenses to a Dedicated Host

terms.definition: The lifecycle state of a Spot Instance request. Key statuses: 'open' (waiting for capacity), 'fulfilled' (instance launched), 'cancelled' (user cancelled), 'closed' (completed normally).
terms.example: A Spot request shows 'open' when no capacity is available at the requested price

terms.definition: A payment option for Savings Plans and Reserved Instances where you pay the full commitment amount at the start of the term. Provides the highest discount.
terms.example: Paying $1,200 upfront at the start of a 1-year Savings Plan instead of $110/month

terms.definition: A payment option for Savings Plans and Reserved Instances where you pay nothing at purchase — charged monthly. Provides the lowest discount among commitment options.
terms.example: Choosing No Upfront for a Savings Plan so there's no large initial payment

terms.definition: A free AWS tool at calculator.aws that allows you to estimate and compare costs across different pricing models, services, and configurations before committing to purchases.
terms.example: Comparing On-Demand vs 1-year Compute Savings Plan costs for 20 T3.large instances

terms.definition: A payment option where you pay part of the commitment cost upfront and the remainder in monthly installments. Discount level falls between All Upfront and No Upfront.
terms.example: Paying $600 upfront and $50/month for a 1-year Savings Plan

terms.definition: An AWS tool that shows the interruption frequency for Spot Instance types, helping you choose pools with historically low interruption rates.
terms.example: Checking that t3.medium has <5% interruption rate before selecting it for a Spot Fleet

terms.definition: A group of EC2 instance types with the same base hardware design and performance characteristics but different sizes. Examples: T3 (burstable), C5 (compute-optimized), M5 (general purpose).
terms.example: EC2 Instance Savings Plan for the T3 family covers t3.micro, t3.small, t3.medium, t3.large, etc.

terms.definition: The historical time window AWS uses to calculate Savings Plan recommendations. Options are typically 7, 30, or 60 days of past usage data.
terms.example: Using a 30-day lookback period to get recommendations based on last month's typical usage

terms.definition: In a Spot Fleet, the total number of instances or vCPUs you want the fleet to maintain. AWS automatically provisions instances to meet this target.
terms.example: Setting target capacity to 10 instances in a Spot Fleet for a batch processing cluster
